Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for your time during last week's screening call. As part of our procurement bar we need a concise mapping of cross-border transfers and the legal mechanisms you rely on (e.g., SCCs, DPF, BCRs) for EU-originating personal data. Our security/compliance reviewers also asked for:

- A per-data-category transfer map (e.g., logs, telemetry, prompts/outputs, support transcripts) showing where data is stored/transferred.
- The primary legal basis under GDPR for processing (contractual performance, legitimate interests, etc.).
- Whether Redwood is registered under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) or relies on SCCs; if both, please clarify the ordering and customer choice.
- Retention windows for logs and debug artifacts for EU customers (by default and for enterprise customers when contractually specified).
- Any supplementary technical/organizational measures you apply when transferring EU data to the US.

I've attached our RFP question spreadsheet (tab: Privacy & Transfers). Can you return the completed mapping and a draft DPA annex we can review?

We'd like to receive this by COB Monday, Dec 7 if possible. If it's easier, happy to set a 30-minute technical deep-dive.

Amanda —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached are two artifacts to start: a CSV export of our current per-data-category transfer mapping and a draft DPA annex with the standard contractual clauses referenced. High level answers below; please see attachments for row-level detail.

High-level summary (quick bullets):
- Transfer mechanisms: Redwood is registered with the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) as of Q3 2026 and also offers the EU SCCs (2021) in our DPA annex. Customers can opt to rely on SCCs in place of DPF where required by procurement/legal policies.
- Ordering/choice: By default we include DPF language in our contract set; if a customer requires SCCs we append the SCC addendum and execute the DPA annex with SCCs. We treat both as contractually equivalent options — customer choice documented at signing.
- Data mapping highlights: Primary storage for model logs and embeddings for EU tenants is in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1; transient processing occurs on US hosts for some model shards and inference accelerators (us-central-1) when certain hosted models are used. See attached CSV for category-level flows.
- Legal basis: Processing for the inference API is primarily performance of a contract and processing necessary for the provision of the service; analytics/telemetry is covered under legitimate interests with an opt-out via contract/per-customer configuration where required.
- Retention: Default retention for debug logs is 30 days for hosted trial tiers, 90 days for standard paid tiers, and configurable up to customer-specified contractual limits for enterprise customers (we can commit to specific windows in the DPA annex).
- Supplementary measures: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, per-tenant encryption keys (KMS-backed), strict access controls with role-based access and audit logs, and KV/prefix caching minimization for EU-only tenants. We also offer a disk-encryption/hsm option for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Next steps:
- We can update the attached CSV with any additional categories you add to the spreadsheet.
- If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute session next week with our infra and legal engineers to walk the mapping line-by-line.

Amanda —

Thanks for the follow-up and the spreadsheet. Per Evelyn's note and our internal follow-ups, please find consolidated answers below plus pointers to the attachments and our next steps. Apologies for the longer message; we've tried to make this actionable for legal and security review.

1) Audit logs and backups
- Default: Audit and access logs for EU tenants are stored in eu-west-1 (primary) with cross-region replication to eu-central-1 for resilience.
- Backups: We do not replicate logs or customer data to US regions by default. Replication to US hosts only occurs when a customer requests a multi-region/high-availability configuration that includes US regions; such replication is documented and contractually controlled.

2) Telemetry and content seeding
- Product telemetry: Aggregation is limited to operational metrics and anonymized usage signals. We do not use raw customer prompts or outputs for model training or telemetry-driven product experimentation for EU tenants by default. Customers can opt-in to a training/analytics program with explicit consent and contractual terms.

3) Transfer mechanisms and contract text
- DPF & SCCs: Redwood is registered under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) as of 2026-09-15. We also support the EU SCCs (2021) in our DPA annex. Our standard approach: include DPF registration details in the DPA and offer SCCs as an alternative contractual mechanism; if a customer requires SCCs we will execute the SCC addendum and include the full SCC text and per-customer data-flow appendix.
- We will add a one-page table in the DPA annex that clarifies which mechanism is in effect per-signature and captures the customer's explicit choice.

4) Retention defaults and contractual flexibility
- Hosted trial tier: debug/log retention = 30 days.
- Standard paid tier: debug/log retention = 90 days.
- Enterprise: configurable via DPA annex; we can commit to specific windows (e.g., 180 days, 365 days) per negotiation.

5) Supplementary technical/organizational measures
- AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, KMS-backed customer key support, role-based access with timebound privileged sessions, structured redaction for support transcripts, and optional disk-encryption/HSM where deployed on Dedicated/Private.
- We also provide per-route caching controls and can disable prefix-KV caching for EU-only tenants to minimize cross-border leakage.

Attachments provided: redwood_privacy_mapping_v1.csv (category-level map), redwood_dpa_annex_draft.pdf (DPA + SCC addendum), crossborder_flow_diagram.svg (infrastructure flow).

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether Healtheon would like us to: (A) proceed with the SCC addendum for your review, (B) rely on DPF and provide proof of registration plus the DPF privacy notice link, or (C) indicate both and let legal pick on signature.
- If helpful, we can schedule a targeted 30-minute technical Q&A (infra + security) to walk through the CSV rows.
